API tokens

Mint, scope, edit, revoke and delete the bearer tokens that let external systems call the /api/v1 integration API.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereAdministrator → API Tokens (every ADOM whose product has the API Tokens capability) (URL /api-tokens/)

What is it?#

An API token is a credential for a machine, not a person. External systems (a SIEM, a ticketing workflow, a CMDB) send it in an Authorization: Bearer <token> header to call SATOM's versioned integration API under /api/v1. Each token is owned by a real SATOM user, bound to one ADOM, limited by a scope and optionally narrowed further by capabilities and an AppID scope. This page is where an administrator issues and manages them; what the API itself offers is described in the API reference.

What does it do?#

  • Create a token and show the full secret exactly once.
  • List every token with its owner, scopes, capabilities, AppID scope, ADOM, status (active, expired, revoked) and when it was last used.
  • Edit a live token's name, ADOM, scopes, capabilities, AppID scope and expiry. The secret itself can never be shown or changed again.
  • Revoke a token (it stays in the list, greyed out, and stops working).
  • Delete a token (the row is removed).
  • Every one of these writes an entry to the audit log.

Requirements#

  • The owner must be an active SATOM user. Only active users are offered in the Owner list.
  • The ADOM you bind the token to must have the API Tokens capability ticked in Settings → ADOMs (see Settings). Only those ADOMs appear in the ADOM list. On a fresh install every shipped ADOM, including global, has it.
  • To use an AppID scope, the AppIDs must exist and be active under AppIDs, with server policies assigned to them.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Every route on this page requires users.manage (the legacy user_manage gate) — in practice the Administrator profile. A user without it gets 403 Forbidden if they open /api-tokens/ directly. The sidebar entry is rendered inside the Administrator group of every ADOM whose product has the API Tokens capability; that group is itself hidden from users without users.manage.

The token never exceeds its owner's permissions. This is checked twice: when the token is created or edited, a scope whose permission the owner does not hold is refused; and on every API call, the owner must still hold it:

Token scope Owner must still hold Lets the token…
read view (any of the view permissions, e.g. appliances.view) call the read (GET) endpoints
write config_write (e.g. protection.edit) run actions and the object-write endpoints
admin user_manage (users.manage) reserved for admin-level reads (see Advanced)

Scopes are ranked read < write < admin: holding write also satisfies an endpoint that needs read.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: a token can no longer be created or edited with a scope its owner's permissions do not cover, the admin scope is honoured only while the owner holds users.manage, the API Tokens link appears in every token-capable ADOM (not only FortiWeb), and Revoke and Delete ask for confirmation.

How to use#

  1. 1CreateFill in name, owner, ADOM, scopes; optionally capabilities and AppIDs
  2. 2CopyThe full token is shown once — store it in your secret manager
  3. 3UseThe external system sends Authorization: Bearer &lt;token&gt;
  4. 4MaintainEdit scope or expiry, revoke or delete when no longer needed

Create a token#

  1. Open Administrator → API Tokens (in the FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator or Global ADOM, whichever has the API Tokens capability).
  2. In the Create a token card, fill in: - Name — a label, e.g. siem-integration (required in the form). - Owner (inherits RBAC) — the user whose permissions cap the token. - ADOM — the product the token is bound to. - Expires (days) — leave empty for a token that never expires.
  3. Tick one or more Scopes. read is ticked by default; if you untick all of them the token is saved with read.
  4. Optionally open Capabilities (what kinds of action) and AppID scope (where) — see Configuration. Each is a dropdown of checkboxes: capabilities grouped by area with their description, AppIDs with a filter box. The button lists what is ticked.
  5. Click Create token.
  6. A green banner appears: New token created — copy it now. This is the only time the full token is shown. Store it securely. Copy the value from the read-only field. Below it the banner repeats the owner, scopes, capabilities, AppID scope and ADOM.

⚠️Warning

SATOM stores only a one-way hash of the secret. If the token is lost, there is no way to display it again — create a new one and delete the old one.

Edit a token#

  1. In Existing tokens, click Edit on the token's row.
  2. In the Edit token dialog change any of Name, ADOM, Expiry (days), Scopes, Capabilities or AppID scope. For Expiry (days): - leave it blank to keep the current expiry (the hint shows it); - enter a number to set the expiry that many days from today; - enter -1 to remove the expiry (never expires).
  3. Click Save changes. The flash message reads Token “<name>” updated.

The owner of a token cannot be changed. To move a token to another owner, create a new token and delete the old one.

Revoke a token#

Click Revoke on the row and confirm "Revoke token '<name>'? Every client using it stops working immediately." The token stops authenticating immediately, its status badge turns to revoked and the Revoke button disappears. The flash message reads Token “<name>” revoked. A revoked token can still be edited but cannot be reactivated.

Delete a token#

Click Delete on the row and confirm "Delete token '<name>'? This cannot be undone." The flash message reads Token deleted.

Use the token#

Send it as a bearer header on every call:

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer fmk_<public-id>_<secret>" \
     https://satom.example.com/api/v1/ping

/api/v1/ping answers with the token's name, owner, scopes, capabilities, AppID scope and ADOM, which is the quickest way to check what a token can do. The full endpoint list is in the API reference.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Name Free label, up to 128 characters. Saved as unnamed if the server receives it empty. Yes (form) siem-integration
Owner (inherits RBAC) Active user whose permissions cap the token. Shown as username (role). Yes svc-siem (operator)
ADOM Product the token is bound to. A token bound to global may act on any product; any other ADOM restricts it to that product. Yes fortiweb
Expires (days) Days from now until the token expires. Empty = never. No 90
Scopes read (GET), write (run actions / config_write), admin. Yes (defaults to read) read, write
Capabilities Allow-list of action kinds. See the table below. No backend_edit
AppID scope Allow-list of AppIDs; the token may only touch server policies bound to them. Empty = no restriction. No APP-0042

Capabilities (labels as shown on the page):

Capability Page description Granted by an empty list?
backend_edit enable/disable pool backends Yes
backend_config change a backend IP / port Yes
policy_status enable/disable server policies Yes
cert_swap swap a policy's certificate Yes
cert_renew renew Server / Client / Client+Server certificates (Cert Manager) No — explicit
maintenance backups / sync / deep capture / signature collect (fleet) Yes
reports stats / inventory / health / HA checks (read-only, fleet) Yes
monitoring deep-monitor sweep, metrics scrape, monitoring report No — explicit
sentinel Sentinel correlate, baselines, CVE mirror refresh, blocklist feed publish No — explicit
feeds signature freshness, knowledge packs, WAF artifact index No — explicit
api_library API library harvests (endpoint evidence, CLI schema, watch) No — explicit
netbox NetBox inventory reconcile No — explicit
waf_exception_draft FILE a FortiWeb WAF carve-out (desired state only — never touches a device) No — explicit only
waf_exception_apply PUSH a filed FortiWeb carve-out onto the appliance No — explicit only
adc_rule_draft PREVIEW a FortiADC carve-out (never touches a device) No — explicit only
adc_rule_apply CREATE a FortiADC carve-out on the appliance No — explicit only
inventory ASK a device its running firmware, live (reads the device, writes only this inventory) No — explicit only

When no capability is ticked, the list column shows every action that needs no explicit grant: the token may run every non-destructive catalog action its scope allows except those of the explicit capabilities. Those must be ticked by name, with one exception kept from before 2026-10-15: a token owned by a user administrator, with nothing ticked, still runs the catalog actions of the six explicit catalog capabilities (cert_renew, monitoring, sentinel, feeds, api_library, netbox), as it did when they had no capability. The object writes and inventory always need the tick.

❗Important

The object-write capabilities only work on a matching ADOM: waf_exception_* needs a fortiweb (or global) token, adc_rule_* needs a fortiadc (or global) token. A FortiWeb-bound token can never write FortiADC rules, even if the capability is ticked.

Example#

🧪Example — A token that may only toggle backends of two applications

A load-balancer automation must be able to take pool members in and out of service for applications APP-0042 and APP-0057, and nothing else.

  1. Create a user svc-lb with an operator-level profile (it needs config_write for the write scope).
  2. Create a token: Name lb-automation, Owner svc-lb, ADOM fortiweb, Expires (days) 180, Scopes write.
  3. Tick only the capability backend_edit.
  4. In AppID scope select APP-0042 and APP-0057.
  5. Create a scheduled action Enable / disable a backend (pool member) for each pool member (see Scheduled actions); the automation triggers them through POST /api/v1/actions/<id>/run.

The token can now run only backend enable/disable actions whose target server policy is bound to one of those two AppIDs. A fleet-wide action (a backup, a health check) is refused with not_appid_scopable; an action on another application's policy is refused with appid_scope_denied.

Result#

  • The token row appears in Existing tokens with the masked form fmk_<public-id>_••••••••, owner, scopes, capabilities, AppID scope, ADOM, an active badge and Last used = never.
  • Last used updates when the token is used (at most about once a minute).
  • The audit log records api_token.create, api_token.edit, api_token.revoke or api_token.delete with the token's public id as the target. Actions performed with the token (running an action, filing a carve-out, a live firmware check, and the refusals of those) are audited under api.* action names, with the token and its owner in the detail (the User column itself normally shows anonymous, because no one is signed in to the console for a token call). Plain read calls such as /api/v1/ping are not audited.

Troubleshooting#

"Choose a valid owner for the token."#

Possible causes - No owner was submitted, or the selected user no longer exists.

Solution 1. Reload the page so the Owner list is current. 2. Pick an active user and create the token again.

Verification - The green New token created banner appears.

A scope is refused when creating or editing a token#

Possible causes - The owner's profile does not contain the permission the scope maps to (see the table under Permissions), for example write for a read-only owner or admin for an owner without users.manage.

Solution 1. Untick that scope, or give the owner the needed permission in Users and profiles, or pick an owner who holds it.

Verification - The token is saved and its row lists the intended scopes.

"Invalid product."#

Possible causes - The ADOM chosen is no longer offered for tokens (its API Tokens capability was switched off, or the ADOM was deactivated, after the page was loaded).

Solution 1. Reload the page and pick an ADOM from the refreshed list. 2. If the ADOM you need is missing, an administrator must tick its API Tokens capability in Settings → ADOMs.

Verification - The ADOM appears in the ADOM drop-down.

The external system gets 401 invalid_token#

Possible causes - The token was revoked, deleted or has expired (status badge revoked or expired, or the row is gone). - The value was copied incompletely; a token always has the shape fmk_<public-id>_<secret>.

Solution 1. Check the token's status in Existing tokens. 2. If it expired, edit it and set a new Expiry (days) (or -1); if it was revoked or lost, create a new token.

Verification - GET /api/v1/ping with the token returns "ok": true.

The external system gets 403 owner_disabled or 403 owner_forbidden#

Possible causes - owner_disabled: the token's owner was deactivated. - owner_forbidden: the owner's profile no longer contains the permission the scope maps to (for example a write token whose owner lost every config-write permission).

Solution 1. Re-enable the owner or restore the needed permission in Users and profiles, or 2. Create a new token owned by a suitable user and delete the old one.

Verification - GET /api/v1/ping succeeds and the intended call no longer returns 403.

The external system gets 403 insufficient_scope or capability_denied#

Possible causes - The endpoint needs a higher scope than the token holds. - The token has a capability list that does not include the action, or the call is an object write and the explicit capability was never ticked.

Solution 1. Edit the token and tick the missing scope or capability.

Verification - GET /api/v1/ping lists the new scope or capability.

Advanced#

Advanced How a token is stored and checked
  • The plaintext has the form fmk_<public-id>_<secret>. The 16-character public id is stored in clear (it is what the list shows); the secret is stored only as a scrypt hash and compared on each call.
  • On each /api/v1 call SATOM looks the token up by public id, rejects it if it is revoked or expired, verifies the secret, checks the owner is active, checks the endpoint's scope and that the owner still holds the RBAC permission mapped to that scope, then binds the request to the token's ADOM.
  • Because the owner check happens at call time, disabling a user or removing their permission neuters all of their tokens immediately, without touching the tokens.
  • /api/v1 is CSRF-exempt (tokens carry no CSRF) and is separate from the session-authenticated internal API used by the web interface.
  • Destructive firmware actions (upgrade, flash, reboot) and any catalog action flagged as dangerous are refused for every token, whatever its scope.
  • Device-changing requests made by a token run inline; they are not wrapped in a job the way browser requests are.
Advanced The `admin` scope

No /api/v1 endpoint is gated on the admin scope as a whole. It is consulted only inside the WAF carve-out endpoints, where it lets a token list or read carve-outs authored by other tokens (GET /api/v1/waf/exceptions?all=1). That check honours admin only when the owner also holds user_manage; a token whose owner lost users.manage sees only its own carve-outs. Tokens can be given admin only if their owner holds users.manage.

Advanced AppID scope rules
  • A token with an AppID scope may run only the per-policy capabilities (backend_edit, backend_config, policy_status, cert_swap). Every other action is refused with not_appid_scopable.
  • SATOM resolves the action's target server policy and requires it to belong to one of the token's AppIDs in the token's ADOM. If the target cannot be resolved (shared pool, content-routing-only pool, cache not yet filled) the call is refused with appid_scope_unresolved — it fails closed.
  • The AppID picker lists active AppIDs of every product; only those of the token's ADOM ever resolve.
